summary:
Turn 29 confirmed the third claim and, after two rejected resolution paths, recorded the precise route that remains for closing the older scope issue.

What was established. Claim C3-applied-effect-follows-committed-vector is now confirmed in scope: its artifact 52a176deb66c4588a59d71f8afeb13ab (executed as ef136d1e25924ce59ccedc4fe9e2af2e) reports violated and its correspondence review found no issue, so the observation that replicas apply different effects for one instance (peer 04 against (void) at the recoverer and the third replica) is attributed to C3 rather than to C1.

What the framework rejected, recorded so it is not repeated. My first attempt to resolve the open scope issue ef6b54abce294555b31a3c9a6ca606ac by attaching a resolution to the new C3 artifact was refused because a resolution must address an issue on the artifact under review or its lineage. Attempting the resolution on the disputed C1 artifact itself was refused because a scope-challenged issue needs a new artifact with the challenged component actually changed and a matching fresh execution. Then a revise_check that dropped the applied-state property was refused twice: an ordinary repair must preserve the claim, oracle, prerequisites and legality, and an encoding correction needs an oracle or observation challenge rather than a scope challenge. The available mechanisms are therefore F2 (a semantic revision of the C1 unit's scope through an attributed feedback file) or a fresh C1 check whose plan carries only the three in-scope properties, so that a later review can resolve the issue against that artifact.

Effect on the findings. Nothing in the three confirmed claims changes: C1 rests on its three in-scope properties (adoption at the resolution, the recoverer-versus-committed-peer comparison, and agreement after the Commit broadcast), C2 on the stable-store record, and C3 on the applied-state observation. The open issue is an attribution bookkeeping item, not a substantive disagreement, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
